report.summary: Host WS-MKT-09 experienced an active compromise where cmd.exe spawned certutil.exe to download an external file from 192.0.2.44 into C:\Users\Public\a.txt, decode it into an executable payload at C:\Users\Public\a.exe, and execute the resulting binary. The external IP address 192.0.2.44 matches a past true-positive alert.

claims.text: The alerting tool EDR reported that certutil was used with network and decode arguments on host WS-MKT-09.
Process cmd.exe (PID 8100) spawned certutil.exe (PID 8110) to download a file from external IP 192.0.2.44 to C:\Users\Public\a.txt via URL cache.
Certutil.exe (PID 8120) was executed via cmd.exe to decode C:\Users\Public\a.txt into an executable payload at C:\Users\Public\a.exe.
The decoded binary C:\Users\Public\a.exe (PID 8130) was executed by cmd.exe (PID 8100).
Indicator IP 192.0.2.44 appeared in past alert PA-2026-1108 which was resolved as a true positive.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-MKT-09 immediately from the network to prevent further staging or lateral movement.
Collect and preserve process memory, disk artifacts, and event logs from WS-MKT-09, specifically targeting C:\Users\Public\a.txt, C:\Users\Public\a.exe, and any spawned child processes.
Block outbound network traffic to the malicious IP address 192.0.2.44 across perimeter firewalls and proxies.
Perform enterprise-wide threat hunting for past or concurrent executions of certutil.exe utilizing the -urlcache and -decode arguments.
Tune detection rules to alert on suspicious command-line patterns involving certutil downloading and decoding files into user-writable directories like C:\Users\Public\.
